rv.q: Funny, shocking, thought-provoking, controversial, superbly staged (Nick Hytner) and performed, this play is all that theatre should be.
This is a terrific piece of work all round, that’s already been showered with Olivier and Critic’s Circle awards.
There are laughs and there are gasps as John Lithgow's sometimes delightful, sometimes horrible, always compelling Roald Dahl fills the air with his nonsense.
What does come out is pretty spectacular.
The play is “subtle, intelligent and stylishly crafted”.

Giant confronts the vile antisemitism of one of the most beloved children's authors of all time, while sweeping along in its ferocious cross-currents of dialogue all the pitched battles of society today
The play is “shocking and impressive” for Patrick Marmion.
Lithgow is never less than riveting in a towering performance.
Dave Fargnoli thinks Rosenblatt’s writing “could be tighter and more sharply focused”
Claire Allfree reckons it reduces each of its characters to “a mouthpiece for a certain point of view”.
They each get their moment to shine – and deserve to bask in a by turns lightly enjoyable and powerfully serious-minded summer smash.

cn.t: Rosenblatt's bold, urgent drama about Roald Dahl's controversial views earns acclaim for tackling difficult subject matter head-on. Lithgow's blistering performance as the irascible, flawed author anchors this massively successful production.
